headline: Wispr Flow launches Notetaker, an AI meeting assistant for Mac users, expanding beyond dictation
summary: Wispr Flow's new AI-powered Notetaker is now available for Mac users, marking the company's expansion into meeting assistance beyond its core dictation services.
details: Wispr Flow has officially launched Notetaker, a new AI-powered meeting assistant now available for Mac users. This marks a significant expansion for the company, moving beyond its established dictation services.

Notetaker is designed to streamline meeting workflows by automatically capturing and processing information. It aims to provide comprehensive assistance for users looking to enhance their productivity during virtual and in-person discussions.

headline_marked: [[SpaceX is coming for T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon]]
headline: SpaceX is coming for T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon
summary: SpaceX plans to build a terrestrial mobile network, aiming to acquire customers from T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon. The company intends to leverage EchoStar spectrum and next-gen Starlink Mobile V2 satellites for a '100 times better' service.
details: SpaceX is preparing to build a terrestrial mobile network, directly challenging major US carriers like T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon. President Gwynne Shotwell and CEO Elon Musk announced this during the company's first earnings call, stating an intent to "acquire quite a few" of their customers.

The company will utilize spectrum acquired from EchoStar, which includes terrestrial components, to establish this network. Shotwell confirmed plans to build out the necessary ground-based hardware and systems to deliver a "true mobile service."

SpaceX already operates "Starlink Mobile," a direct-to-device service that provides limited messaging and data in cellular dead zones. The new, expanded service, leveraging EchoStar bandwidth and next-generation Starlink Mobile (V2) satellites set to fly next year, is anticipated to be "100 times better."

Despite acquiring only 65 megahertz of spectrum from EchoStar, significantly less than the Big 3 carriers, SpaceX has innovative deployment strategies. Shotwell hinted at using Starlink broadband dishes as "little femtocells" to efficiently build a ground-based network.

These small cellular base stations, integrated with Starlink dishes, could be deployed on the roofs of houses and businesses across the country. This approach aims to provide better and higher bandwidth connectivity directly to cellphones on the ground, bypassing the need for expensive, large cellular base stations.

The US wireless market is estimated to be worth around $600 billion annually. SpaceX's broader ambitions to sell mobile contracts directly to individuals in the US had been rumored prior to its IPO, now officially confirmed.
